newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA SPOIL JUVENTUS'S TITLE CELEBRATIONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA SPOIL JUVENTUS'S TITLE CELEBRATIONS.

text.p: Parma spoiled the party for 50,000 Juventus supporters on Sunday when they drew 1-1 to prevent the European Cup finalists clinching their 24th serie A title at Turin's Delle Alpi Stadium.

Instead of erupting in a chorus of cheers, Juventus fans whistled and jeered their players after a lacklustre second half in which neither side took risks for fear of being caught on the counter-attack.

"We've been trying to win the title since the first day of the season, so while I understand our fans, they'll just have to be a little more patient," Juve coach Marcello Lippi said after his 100th league game with the club.
But the party for Juventus, who are celebrating their 100th anniversary this year, was surely merely delayed.
The Turin club need only a draw in their next match at Atalanta or in their last game against Lazio to lift their second "scudetto", or little shield, in three seasons.
Then there is the potential partying after the European Cup final against Germany's Borussia Dortmund later this month when Juventus can clinch their second successive continental title.
"But we've first got to win the league title, then we'll think about the European Cup," said Fiat car tycoon Gianni Agnelli, whose family owns Juventus.
Parma looked the better side early on and were rewarded in the 29th minute when Juve's French playmaker Zinedine Zidane deflected a shot by Argentina's Nestor Sensini past his own goalkeeper.
But Juventus drew level 12 minutes later through a Nicola Amoruso penalty awarded after Italy striker Christian Vieri was fouled by fellow international Fabio Cannavaro.
Parma players erupted in protest at the decision along with coach Carlo Ancelotti, who was shown a red card.
"The penalty was not there -- plain and simple. And I don't know why I was thrown out, either, since I did not lose my calm and was quite composed," Ancelotti said.
The draw kept Parma two points ahead of Internazionale, held 1-1 at Roma, and kept alive their hopes of taking part in next season's European Cup.
Elsewhere, Sampdoria's long-dormant attack came alive to beat Udinese 4-0 in a key showdown for a spot in next season's UEFA Cup, in which four Italian teams will participate.

Promising striker Vincenzo Montella, who is set to partner newly-signed Juergen Klinsmann in attack next season, scored twice for Sampdoria and, with 20 goals, is just one behind top scorer Filippo Inzaghi of Atalanta.
The win gave the Genoa club sole possession of fifth place on 49 points, one fewer than Lazio who came back to draw 2-2 at AC Milan to grab a point vital to their UEFA Cup hopes.

Liberian George Weah had put Milan ahead in the 29th and again in the 74th minute but the champions' hopes of clinching a spot in the UEFA Cup next season were virtually killed off when Czech Pavel Nedved equalised for Lazio four minutes from time.

UEFA Cup finalists Internazionale stayed in the hunt for a place in next season's Champions' League thanks to their French playmaker Youri Djorkaeff, who came off the bench to score a brilliant late equaliser against Roma.
Perugia, struggling to avoid relegation, triumphed 4-1 at relegated Reggiana to pull level on 34 points with Cagliari and Piacenza, who drew 1-1 with one another.
Two of those three teams are likely to drop into the second division with Reggiana and Verona, who became the second club condemned to relegation when they drew 1-1 with Atalanta.
Perugia travel to Piacenza for their final match in what could be a decisive battle to stay in the top flight.
